extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys/agents, and USPTO examiners (TC2800) involved in ex parte appeals and pre-appeal practice
extracted.subtask_short: USPTO ex parte pre-appeal & appeal practice
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and procedural standards for requesting and handling USPTO pre-appeal conferences and ex parte appeals (notice/briefing, panel review, timelines, and argument design), with examples of appropriate vs. appeal-level issues. Focused on Technology Center 2800 practice but reflects cited PTO regs and case law.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to Request a Pre-Appeal Conference
rubrics_metrics.description: Circumstances in which a Pre-Appeal Conference should be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request a Pre-Appeal Conference if some or all rejections of record are improper and without basis, are based on a factual or legal error, or when filing an Appeal might be better. Also consider if the rejections articulate a prima facie case that requires further evidence or interpretation of the claims or the applied art to rebut.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-Appeal Request Form & Submission Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Form and content rules for submitting a Pre-Appeal Brief Request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use USPTO Form PTO/SB/33 or label your request 'Pre-Appeal Brief Request For Review'. Submit WITH the Notice of Appeal as a SEPARATE document. No amendments, affidavits, or other evidence may be submitted with the request. No request fee (but Notice of Appeal fee still required). Attach no more than five (5) pages of arguments. Arguments should be CLEAR, CONCISE, and FOCUSED.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-Appeal Panel Composition and Decision Timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Who reviews Pre-Appeal requests and how quickly a decision is expected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technology Center convenes a panel; TC2800 uses a QAS (Quality Assurance Specialist), SPE, and the examiner of record. The panel reviews identified rejections, the arguments submitted, and the file. The panel will decide if an issue for appeal is present and issue a decision which should be mailed within 45 days of receipt of a properly filed request. No applicant or representative participation in the panel review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design of Pre-Appeal: 'Clear Deficiency' Standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard the Pre-Appeal panel uses to find a Pre-Appealable issue: a clear deficiency in the prima facie case supporting a rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of 'clear deficiency' include (1) clearly improper rejections based upon an error in fact, and (2) omission of essential elements required for a prima facie rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of Arguments Appropriate for Pre-Appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Types of arguments that are suited to the limited Pre-Appeal (≤5 pages) review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appropriate Pre-Appeal arguments include: the applied reference is not in fact prior art; the inventive entity is clearly not one to which the reference can be applied; a claim element is clearly not present in the applied art; support in the disclosure is clearly found contrary to a 112(a) rejection (contrary to the rejection’s assertion); no rationale is provided in a 103 rejection; no evidentiary basis for a 103 rationale is provided in the rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issues More Appropriate for Full Appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples of issues that typically exceed Pre-Appeal scope and are better addressed in an Appeal brief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arguments likely to take more than five pages and better suited for Appeal include: secondary considerations, improper combinations/teaching away in 103 rejections, unsettled or challenging case law analysis, questions over the broadest reasonable interpretation (BROI), challenges to Official Notice or inherency findings, and characteristics of the POSITA rendering 103 improper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Possible Pre-Appeal Panel Decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Enumerated dispositions the Pre-Appeal panel may issue regarding the claims under review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The panel's decision will state one of: application remains under appeal; prosecution is reopened; application is allowed; or request is noncompliant and is dismissed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post Pre-Appeal Options / Next Steps
rubrics_metrics.description: Permissible applicant actions following a Pre-Appeal decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depending on outcome, options include proceeding by filing an appeal brief, taking indicated allowable material (amend claims), filing a Request for Continued Examination (RCE) or a continuation, or abandoning the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal Conference Process and Examiner Handling
rubrics_metrics.description: How cases are handled at the Technology Center after an appeal is filed and before PTAB docketing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Case goes to the examiner’s amended docket and the examiner requests a conference with the SPE and QAS. The conferees hold a conference and the conference decision is to prepare an Examiner’s Answer or reopen prosecution (issue a new rejection or allow).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-Appeal vs Appeal — Filing Times, Page Limits, Conferees, Decision Goals
rubrics_metrics.description: Comparative procedural differences between a Pre-Appeal request and a regular Appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing times: Pre-Appeal is same day as Notice of Appeal (filed with Notice); Appeal Brief due two months from Notice of Appeal (extendable for five months per 37 C.F.R. § 41.37(a) and 41.45(c)). Page limit: Pre-Appeal arguments limited to 5 pages; Appeal briefs have different/longer briefing requirements. Conferees: both processes involve examiner, SPE, and QAS. Decision goals: Pre-Appeal generally ≤45 days; Appeal conference decisions generally ≤56 days (per slide guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Argument Ordering and Strategy: Best Argument First
rubrics_metrics.description: Tactical guidance on ordering arguments in Pre-Appeal or Appeal submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order arguments with the best argument first. Use a 'Funnel Approach' to structure each issue: Rejection → Claim → Limitation → Why (i.e., identify the rejection at issue, the claim at issue, the limitation at issue, and explain why it is erroneous).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to Explain Why Examiner Erred and Waiver Rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Mandatory content and consequence for omissions in appellant submissions (statutory/regulatory guidance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Per 37 C.F.R. § 41.37(c)(1)(iv): 'The arguments shall explain why the examiner erred as to each ground of rejection contested by appellant.' The Board will treat as waived, for purposes of the present appeal, any arguments not raised by appellant (77 Fed. Reg. 72270, 72275).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid Mere Recitation; Must Argue Separate Patentability
rubrics_metrics.description: What does not qualify as an argument for patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A statement which merely points out what a claim recites will not be considered an argument for separate patentability of the claim (37 C.F.R. § 41.37(c)(1)(iv)). See also In re Lovin, 652 F.3d 1349 (Fed. Cir. 2011). Parties must explain why the elements recited render the claim patentable over the rejection, not merely repeat claim language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim Interpretation Guidance — Deference to PTO Without Express Definition
rubrics_metrics.description: How claim terms are interpreted when the specification lacks express definitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Absent an express definition in the specification, appellants pointing to definitions or usages that conform to their interpretation does not make the PTO's definition unreasonable where the PTO can point to other sources that support its interpretation (In re Morris, 127 F.3d 1048, 1056 (Fed. Cir. 1997)). To control interpretation, include express definitions in the specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal Filing, Fees, and Regulation Citations
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulatory citations and named filing/fee requirements for appeals and related documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key cited rules and documents: Notice of Appeal + Fee — 37 C.F.R. § 41.31 & § 41.20(b)(1). Appeal Brief — 37 C.F.R. § 41.37; MPEP 1205. Examiner’s Answer — 37 C.F.R. § 41.39; MPEP 1207. Appeal Forwarding Fee — 37 C.F.R. § 41.45 & § 41.20(b)(4). Reply Brief — 37 C.F.R. § 41.41. Oral Hearing Request + Fee — 37 C.F.R. § 41.47 & § 41.20(b)(3); MPEP 1208. Time limits: Appeal Brief due two months from Notice of Appeal (extendable for five months per 37 C.F.R. § 41.37(a) and extension rule 37 C.F.R. § 41.45(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Style Guidance for Pre-Appeal Arguments
rubrics_metrics.description: Concise style and length expectations for Pre-Appeal submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-Appeal arguments should be CLEAR, CONCISE, and FOCUSED and limited to no more than five pages. Use precise, direct statements showing why the examiner erred rather than extended evidentiary submissions or new affidavits (which are not permitted).
